case.title: The Technician filter combines with other filters and Clear all filters
case.custom_preconds:
• Owner/Admin with Work Orders View and Create & Edit permissions; browser at least 1024 px wide. Active, clockable technicians A and B are eligible at this location.
  • Three Approved work orders: WO1 = lead A/customer A; WO2 = lead B/customer A; WO3 = lead A/customer B. Use distinct, searchable customer names.
  • None of these work orders is assigned to the signed-in user as lead technician, line-item technician or service advisor. Customer A has no Paid work orders.
  • Clear filters and search; Assigned to me off.

Source: PRD v60, S1-R15a, S1-R13 and S1-N1a.
case.custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders → All → Tech View. Search for customer A and select technician A.
  2. Turn Assigned to me on.
  3. Turn Assigned to me off.
  4. Apply Status = Paid while keeping the search and Technician selection.
  5. Click Clear all filters.
case.custom_expected:
Step 1: Only WO1 appears: customer search and Technician filter are combined. WO2 and WO3 are excluded.

Step 2: No work orders appear. Show “No work orders match these filters”, “Try removing a filter to widen your results.” and Clear all filters. Assigned to me combines with the existing filters using AND.

Step 3: WO1 returns; search and Technician selection are retained.

Step 4: No work orders appear, with the same no-match message, supporting text and Clear all filters action. Status combines with the other conditions using AND.

Step 5: Technician and Status selections are cleared. WO2 is visible again.

Last checked against build v26.43.0-ffea43c (production) on 10/23/2026.

AUTOMATION: READY

changes.label: Preconditions
changes.old_value:
Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Owner or Admin user whose role has Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit, at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
  • Your browser window is at least 1024 px wide, so the display switcher (List, Tech View, Board View) shows at the right of the Work Orders toolbar.
  • Technician {Technician-A} (for example Esther Howard) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
  • Technician {Technician-B} (for example Ralph Edwards) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
  • Customer {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST NT3 Technician Filter Mix") is used by this case only.
  • Customer {Customer-B} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST NT3 Other Customer") is used by this case only, and its name does not contain {Customer-A}'s name.
  • Approved work order {Work-order-1} (for example S10043-17627) for {Customer-A} is led by {Technician-A}.
  • Approved work order {Work-order-2} (for example S10043-17628) for {Customer-A} is led by {Technician-B}.
  • Approved work order {Work-order-3} (for example S10043-17629) for {Customer-B} is led by {Technician-A}.
  • None of these work orders is assigned to you: you are not their lead technician, not their Service Advisor and not on any of their lines.
  • Status {Status-A} (for example Paid) is a status none of {Customer-A}'s work orders has.
  • On the Work Orders page nothing is chosen in any filter, Assigned to me is off and Search is empty.

changes.label: Steps
changes.old_value:
1. Open Work Orders and click the All tab.
  2. Click Tech View in the display switcher.
  3. Type the name of {Customer-A} in Search.
  4. Click the Technician filter and tick {Technician-A}.
  5. Click outside the Technician filter list to close it.
  6. Read the groups and rows shown.
  7. Turn on Assigned to me.
  8. Read the page.
  9. Turn off Assigned to me.
  10. Read the rows shown.
  11. Click Status and tick {Status-A}.
  12. Click outside the Status list to close it.
  13. Read the page.
  14. Click Clear all filters.
  15. Read the Technician filter, the Status filter and the rows shown.
changes.new_value:
1. Open Work Orders → All → Tech View. Search for customer A and select technician A.
  2. Turn Assigned to me on.
  3. Turn Assigned to me off.
  4. Apply Status = Paid while keeping the search and Technician selection.
  5. Click Clear all filters.

changes.label: Expected Result
changes.old_value:
Expected results

  • Step 6: only {Work-order-1} shows, in {Technician-A}'s group. {Work-order-2} (led by {Technician-B}) and {Work-order-3} (another customer) are not shown.
  • Step 8: no work order shows. The page reads "No work orders match these filters", then "Try removing a filter to widen your results.", with a Clear all filters button.
  • Step 10: {Work-order-1} shows again, still only in {Technician-A}'s group.
  • Step 13: the same empty state shows: "No work orders match these filters", then "Try removing a filter to widen your results.", with a Clear all filters button.
  • Steps 14 and 15: the Technician filter shows nothing chosen, nothing is ticked in Status, and {Work-order-2} shows again in {Technician-B}'s group.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10044 (Story 1, Switch between display options); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 52 (14 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S1-R15a (added in version 52 on 14 Oct 2026, Chris Ward ruling after Sasha Grosman's staging review follow-up), read 14 Oct 2026. Source-verified 14 October 2026. Not yet checked against a build. S1-N1a (reworded in version 43) and S1-R13.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S1-R15a: “The Technician filter combines with every other filter and with Assigned to me: a work order shows only if it matches all of them. When nothing matches, the empty state of S1-N1a applies, and Clear all filters also clears the Technician filter.”
  • S1-R13: “With Assigned to me enabled, show only the work orders that match the existing Assigned to me rules, in every display option.”
  • S1-N1a: “With filters active, with or without a search, the empty state reads “No work orders match these filters”, then “Try removing a filter to widen your results.”, with a Clear all filters button.”
